text: I'm dumbfounded by the rave reviews. This hands-down the worst hotel I've stayed at in New Orleans and we come every single year. To begin with, when we checked in, at 12:30am, we were given keys with the room number of one room. We went there, but our keys didn't work so the porter let us in. I put my daughter to bed, unpacked and crawled into bed myself. My husband went down to the front desk to straighten out the key issue. He returned informing me that the front desk clerk had written down the wrong room number and in fact we were in another room. I called down to complain but the receptionist stated that the room she sent us to is already booked so we can't stay. It's about 1:00am now. So, we pack up our belongings and our sleeping daughter (3 1/2 yrs old) and move to another room; at least the porter helped us that time. We get to the new room and it is like a coffin. The only window in the entire "suite" (and I use this term very liberally here because that's what they call it) is to the hallway. There isn't a single window in the "suite" which opens. It's like a shotgun coffin room. It's incredibly dangerous if there is ever a fire because there is only one exit - the door or window (right next to one another) which opens to a small walkway. The smell in this room is atrocious. It smells like mold. Not surprising since the only ventilation in the room is the AC. I'm pissed, this isn't an inexpensive room, but I'm SO tired so we make our daughter's bed again, and unpack, but while we are unpacking I get this headache that just won't go away. It gets worse and worse. It becomes apparent that the culprit is a powerful mold smell in the room. It smells like a very damp basement. My husband put his foot down and went back down to the reception desk to demand a room without mold. It's about 2:30 am now. It takes about 1/2 an hour for the receptionist to agree to move us BACK to the original room. It seems that the room IS actually available except for the last night of our stay (5 nights). So we move our daughter, repack and move for the third time that night back into the ORIGINAL room. It takes us about 1/2 an hour to repack all our things and haul it across the hotel to the original room. This time we have no porter to help. We remake my daughter's bed, don't even bother unpacking, and fall into bed at about 3:30am. Oh, and they wanted to charge us for the difference between the old room vs. the new room. Here's the irony. When I called down to the receptionist I OFFERED to pay more to stay in the original room, but she LIED to me and told me it wasn't available. After they made us pack and unpack, pack and unpack, and then pack and unpack in the middle of the night moving a 3 1/2 yr old 3 x's I pretty much lost any desire to pay for a non-moldy "upgrade." The receptionist apologized to my husband, but never once offered an apology to me. Also, management never even bother to acknowledge what had happened or apologize. Because we we kept running around the hotel for the whole night we got about 3 hours of sleep our first night and one full day of our vacation in New Orleans was ruined due to exhaustion. We had to come back to the hotel early the next day and nap the entire afternoon just to make up for the 3 hours of sleep we got the night before. The last night they moved us to another room. They moved us FOUR times. Three times to non-suite rooms (when we paid for a suite). Never did anyone offer to move our luggage until the last time when All that being said here's my sum of the hotel: Pros: location (very close to FQ, Aquarium, St. Charles street car, and top notch restaurants like Lüke, Palace Cafe, and Cochon), plunge pool to stay cool in, decent WI-FI ( free & relatively fast) VERY friendly and helpful maid and valet staff (10 thumbs up for these people who do the hardest work and get the least reward!), beautiful old warehouse style hotel reno with exposed berms and high ceilings, and the front desk went around to check it out and the smoke smell quickly went away. I don't know how they resolved it, they never told us, but they did resolve it. Cons: There is no ventilation in any of the rooms, poorly designed and poorly maintained. Even the nicer rooms with a single window to the world outside don't open, and the bathroom vent motors don't work. All the bathroom ceilings I have seen (3 now) have black mold all across them, horrible insulation (we can hear the people above us IPhone ding for messages and can make out their ENTIRE conversations, the breakfast is pretty bad (think reconstituted eggs), lastly (bupper management apathy regarding service and lodging issues. We travel to New Orleans every year and I can promise you I will never come back to this place. Listen to the bad reviews. I wish I had. They have a place that could be a real gem with a little renovation and a big shake up with the reservation staff and upper management.

text: This is an update to my previous posting. I write this review as I sit in my hotel at the courtyard Marriott in downtown Tampa. Checked in in the morning. Had my surgery this afternoon with Drs. Norman and Boone was back in my hotel around 5:30pm with an ice pack that they provided. I received a call from Dr. Boone tonight to check up on me. The surgeons also provide their cell numbers and encourage you to call them if any problems arise or you have any questions. Dr. Norman was attentive and kept me informed even between patients. It's late night and I am watching the 11pm news. I feel like a million bucks. My tiny wound is sore but it is now to the point where I don't feel like I need the ibuprofen. Full disclosure, it was rough when I came out of anesthesia. The wound was really sore. My fingers were cold and tingly, my heart was kind of slow, like WTF! That could have been an anesthesia thing since anesthesia lowers your core body temp. I was given Calcium pills that were fine at first but thereafter I realized the calcium pills were causing the vomiting, even with food. I am working with Dr. Boone to remedy. The ibuprofen and Tylenol helped with pain. I don't think I was quite ready to be discharged by the time they released me. I was a bit unsteady on my feet as I got on the hotel shuttle but I am glad they did release me at that point because I am confident that is why I am feeling awesomely better at this time. There is nothing like being in your own space for recovery. Whatever you do, eat light and stay away from acidic foods on the first day, drink fluids slow and in small quantities on the first day. I drank a glass of water fast and vomited....waste of a good dinner. However, after that, I felt dramatically better. My ankles are normal size. I didn't realize I was retaining fluid when I had these tumors. Look in the mirror about 8 -10 hours after surgery. If you were retaining water, you may see somewhat of a difference after surgery. I don't have my BP monitor with me but I can tell I am within normal range. I'd had such yo-yo uncontrollable blood pressure for so long that I can actually estimate with some accuracy where I am at without taking a reading. Meeting other patients made realize I was not alone. Ladies, this symptom is not on Dr. Norman's website but now that I have chatted with another patient, I am confident it is one. Normally, I exercise and eat healthy small portions. Even up to the surgery I kept my carbs low, and loaded up on veggies and modest amounts of protein. I was not losing weight. I was gaining. Met a Florida patient who was basically told by a previous doctor that her condition was due to menopause, related the same experience. I am sure she feels like a million bucks now. Now, this is really important. About a week before my surgery, one of my docs thought I should seek a second opinion after she spoke to a local endocrine physician who deemed Dr. Norman's perspective on scans as "inflammatory." I had no intention of getting any further opinions mainly because when I did previously, I found myself experiencing everything Dr. Norman's site said one may run into with an inexperienced surgeon. Here's the clincher, I HAD TWO TUMORS! My scan at UCLA did not reveal two tumors and the surgeon was not even sure that the one she did see was a Parathyroid Adenoma even though my labs were conclusive enough for her to diagnose Hyperparathyroidism so she wanted to biopsy the tumor. I declined (read about biopsy warning on the website). Her NP also advised that a resident would perform the surgery under the surgeon's supervision. I declined. This not the surgery you want someone training on you. So really, I wasted a lot of time attending a physician who ran endless tests, scan, ultrasounds and in the end still wasn't sure if what she saw was a Parathyroid Adenoma. So good thing I didn't listen to "inflammatory." If there is one piece of advice I can give you, it is just save yourself the time and expense of going to other surgeons and just go to the Norman Parathyroid Ctr. This is probably the worst economic time of life and my health plan concerns contracts with local physicians but I realized after I was able to get a breakdown of the cost of this surgery between all parties involved that the cost is not even remotely what it would have been at UCLA. I worked it out and I am so glad I did. Big props to Dr. Norman and his team. Read the website! I used that site and its app to self diagnose and now I am free of two tumors and have my life back.

text: Life is full of unpleasant surprises. Such as when you forget to shut off the Sonicare before removing it from your mouth. Or when you spit your gum out the car window only to realize the window wasn't rolled down. Or Marmalade Cafe. With a name as charming as Marmalade Cafe I had high hopes when my lady friend and I decided to enjoy a late lunch there today. I should've known better when I discovered it was in a mall. I've never heard anyone say "You must go to that restaurant so-and-so, it's in the mall and it is DELIGHTFUL." However, since we had some shopping to do at Macy's we figured we might as well give this place a try. Well, the first thing you will ask yourself when you walk through the doors of Marmalade Cafe is "How the Hell did end I up in this tacky McMansion?" The decor had everything you'd expect to find in the suburbs of Houston or Dallas. Wrought iron chairs with overstuffed cushions, distressed paintings of flowers, dark wood ceiling fans with amber-colored lights and trompe-l'oeil on the walls. I half expected a suburban Christian housewife with big hair and too much makeup to be sitting in the corner quietly judging me for my poor life choices. After perusing the menu, my lady friend ordered the turkey melt with fries and an iced tea while I ordered the BLTA with fries and was tempted to order a martini but didn't want someone to think I'm an alcoholic, so I too order the iced tea. Well, it's not a good sign when the average menu price for a lunch item is $15 and your iced tea arrives in a plastic glass. Really, a plastic glass? I had to look around to make sure I hadn't been seated in the children's section by mistake. Even lower budget restaurants like The Natural Cafe have the class to serve my drink in glass. Then the food arrived. To my relief, I knew immediately I wouldn't get food poisoning because clearly all of the food had been previously frozen. Especially the fries. In order to make my BLTA appear substantial, they piled it high with about 6 inches of iceberg lettuce. Firstly, I'm not a rabbit or a tortoise. Secondly, I've never described lettuce as being "leathery" or "chewy" but those are the only words I can use to describe it. After I removed about 5 inches of lettuce, the remaining tomato, bacon and avocado was quite tasty. My lady friend mentioned that her Turkey Melt made her nostalgic because it tasted remarkably like the Hungry Man turkey dinners her dear mother would feed her as a child. Bless her hillbilly heart. The turkey was dry and chewy and we both agreed they should've named the sandwich the Turkey Jerky Melt. Then, much to my horror, as the late afternoon winter sunshine began to stream through the windows, I noticed the spider webs glistening beneath the chair at the table next to us. Mind you, we were NOT eating outside on the patio. We were sitting INSIDE. As we waited for our check, I nervously searched my pocket book for my lighter and a can of hair spray should the black widow who created the webs happen to make an appearance before the bill came. Luckily it did not. After paying the bill, I went to the restroom to do my lady business and wash my hands. It was then that I realized why they named it Marmalade Cafe. Because the restroom floors are sticky, like marmalade. On a positive note, our waiter was very much a gentleman and quite attentive even if he did appear to have a previous criminal record. The rest of the staff looked as though they peaked in high school. If you love yourself, please don't eat at the mall.

text: DO NOT GO TO THIS DENTIST. I'm only sorry I didn't take the time to write this review sooner because I just scrolled down and saw someone else's review that describes an eerily similar experience to what I suffered through. Hopefully people see that review and this one and think twice before making an appointment with Dr. Yurovsky. This happened to me almost 2 years ago now, so the specific dates are fuzzy but the bottom line is this was the worst dental experience I've ever gone through and am now (hopefully understandably) scared to go to a dentist in the future. I was referred to Dr. Yurovsky by a friend of mine. I needed a new dentist because mine relocated and I needed a spot that was accessible by walking/public transportation. At the time of my appointment I had never had a cavity in my life. I went to Dr. Yurovsky for a regular check-up, not because I was having any pain at all. She said that I had 4 cavities (2 on each side in my molars) and that I needed to have them filled. I told her I'd never had a cavity and had no pain at all, but she said I needed to have them filled ASAP so they didn't get worse. She scheduled it in 2 segments - she was going to fill the "cavities" on the right and then a few days later fill the ones on the left. I went in for the appointment and thus embarked 8 months of dental pain, frustration and money. She filled the "cavities" and said the pain should go away in a few hours and I'd be able to chew on it. I was having a ton of pain and it didn't subside and I definitely couldn't chew on the right side of my mouth. I called her and told her I was having a lot of pain and she said I had told her that I'd never had a cavity before so I didn't know what to expect and this was normal. She was unbelievably condescending. I cancelled my appointment to have the left side filled, but the pain didn't go away and I made a second appointment for her to examine me since the right side that she filled was still so uncomfortable and I couldn't chew still. She looked at me, was hugely condescending, and again said everything looked perfect and I was fine. Since she wasn't going to help me, I made an appointment with another dentist who someone else referred me to (keep in mind all of this required my taking time off of work and paying for appointments, work done and transportation). The second dentist said I may not have had cavities at all because there were no cavities on the left side. He said the right side was improperly filled and he had to redo it - try to undo whatever she did and then put in another filling. 2nd charge for cavities that never existed getting filled. Unfortunately this didn't help the pain and I still couldn't chew on the right side of my mouth and it was ongoing discomfort. I went back to the 2nd dentist for another visit and he didn't know why I was in pain and didn't know what to do. I waited a month or 2 and then went for a 3rd appointment because I was so uncomfortable. He said the only thing he could think to do was get a root canal and put a crown on it - not fun or cheap. I made an appointment with an endodontist he recommended to me (more money, more time off work). He said I needed a root canal. I made an appointment and came back to get a root canal but was advised before I went to do a bite test and a temperature test right before getting the root canal done because if it wasn't that painful then I might not need the root canal. The day of the procedure (more money, more time off work) I did the tests and it wasn't painful so the endodontist said to hold off on a root canal because maybe I didn't need it after all. Pain continued, so I went to a THIRD dentist - my mom's dentist, so that meant taking a train from the city up to Bucks County for this. He took a special scope with a camera on the end and showed a fracture in my tooth, probably sustained, he said, during the original filling. He also looked at the original x-rays from Dr. Yurovsky's office and said he didn't see that I'd ever had cavities on the right side at all. He said I should get a root canal and put a crown on it. Back to the city for another appointment with the endodontist (who I should also review negatively because he was so amazingly condescending too but I think one bad review is all I can muster right now). text: The fries were best part of this meal... Womp Womp. It was opening night so we were ready for a decent wait. That being said we waited for over an hour and a half. When it finally did we got our fries first, which came with a side of aioli- they are McDonald's style, maybe a little thinner and pretty delicious. The high hopes we had for our burgers was immediately diminished upon site of the bun- way too big and worst of all it was COLD (like it literally just came out of the fridge). I got a burger with gouda, the special sauce, and an onion ring on top (basically the P'unk burger without the bacon). Let me break it down, a great burger, to me, is all about that perfect balance between the juicy patty, the melty cheese, the crisp lettuce and maybe a tangy pickle in unobtrusive bun that just holds all the goodness together. This burger just tasted like sadness that tried really hard not to be so sad. Between the cold, thick bun, the beef patty was really dense, overcooked to a rubbery texture, overseasoned, and oversalted. The cold bun negated any meltiness the cheese would have had and the "special sauce", managing to be at the same time really acidic and really watery just served as another discordant flavor in this already haphazard burger. To top it off, the onion ring that I'd hoped to bring a nice crunch to the burger was mushy-- not crunchy in the least. That someone labored over this flavor profile and came out with this result leads me to think that it wasn't just a problem with execution, although better execution might have had me writing a slightly less scathing review... I appreciate that they are using organic, hormone free, grass fed beef, and I am all about paying for quality ingredients (base burger starts at $7.95), but all this means nothing if it doesn't taste like a delicious burger at its core. I don't think I'll be back and I would not recommend this place for a burger on Passyunk. Fountain Porter and POPE both have way better burgers for a better price as well. Sorry!

This is a place you go with others who really enjoy innovative cuisine and then you all share a bunch of bites of food with each other and discuss how amazing everything is...while you share a bottle of wine or some craft beer. My 2 favorite dishes of all time have been the short rib gnocchi which we've had multiple times and the squash which we had for the first time this past weekend. I hesitate to order squash because it's usually butternut which can be a bit too sweet and sometimes stringy. We were told this was locally-grown kabocha squash, and it had house-made marshmallow fluff, browned butter-molasses sauce, chile pepper threads, and some sort of salty smoked nuts. Perfect texture for the squash and the toppings were divine and the ideal complement. I wanted to order 3 more plates of it! I'm daydreaming of this squash. Oh, and the desserts are fantastic. The only time anything has been just slightly less than perfect was when we came in during the tail-end of a Cigar City multi-course tasting event. Employees can answer any question you may have about the food, wine, beer, oysters and although you may label them as hipsters, all have been friendly and approachable. The restaurant is quite small, so I'd recommend reservations on weekends or going later in the night. They do have a small parking lot that pretty much matches up with the size of the restaurant. The building is non-descript from the outside but the decor inside is very cool. I love that the lighting fixtures are made from chicken feeders. This is my favorite restaurant in Seminole Heights. I hesitate to give this answer when people ask me, "So if you live there...what's your favorite restaurant?" because I think, "Are they like my family?" But this is it. The problem is that the food I had wasn't good. We were greeted immediately upon entering and sat down quickly. A waitress took our drink orders right away and brought chips with salsa verde. Our food was served within a decent amount of time, but we were not given silverware or napkins and there was no plate for the fajitas - we had to ask for all of it. The fajitas were bland, with no seasoning whatsoever. The steak was crunchy and the peppers were mushy with an acidic aftertaste. The chimichanga was ordered with mole sauce. The mole sauce tasted like thick old coffee and completely covered and saturated the chimichanga. The menus said it would be topped with onions and sour cream. There were no onions and I had to ask for sour cream. The chimichanga itself was bland, lacking in seasoning and flavor. I love authentic refried beans, which is why I ordered them as a side. They tasted as if they came from a can, the consistency was off and like everything else the beans lacked in seasoning and flavor. I am really disappointed. I was really hoping that this could be my new local go-to for a yummy authentic Mexican meal. Unfortunately I'll need to keep looking.

text: Went here for the first time on a whim with my boyfriend, and we were very pleased! Our dumplings came out after not too long of a wait, and they were delicious. Plenty of tender, cheesy dumplings, a fair amount of mushrooms, and two shrimp, all in a delicious sauce. After this, we were both excited for our entrees, and we were not disappointed. My veal saltimbocca came in the form of three healthy sized veal medallions, each topped with a generous slice of proscuitto, melted cheese, and a wonderful sage cream sauce. It wasn't an enormous amount of food, but I was very full after eating it. My boyfriend greatly enjoyed his enormous quantity of mussels, drenched in a delicious red sauce (which we sopped up with bread later). The gnocchi was the lightest and fluffiest I have ever had, without a doubt, and well worth its reputation. I preferred the regular ricotta gnocchi in the gorganzola sauce, but my boyfriend preferred the spinach gnocchi in the red sauce. Both were excellent, but I think either would be a bit much to order as an entree. Overall, a very solid Italian BYOB. I would describe their food in general as "fancy comfort food", in that many of the dishes are more original than a traditional macaroni-and-gravy Italian restaurant (like Villa di Roma), but they aren't the culinary equivalent of haute couture either. We will absolutely be back.

text: For five years, I have been waiting for this city to have a true creperie, a true French restaurant with buckwheat galettes with a side of simple greens that I could enjoy with a glass of wine. And it's finally happened! To say I was overjoyed is an understatement. I hugged the manager and one of the owners, and I smiled the entire time I was there. Absolutely elated. The restaurant is a quaint little place right on the edge of Mass Ave with a classic red and black theme that probably caters more to what Americans think of France, but is 100% adorable. There is a small bar to get wine, beer, cocktails, or coffee, and several small tables with a tiny lounge area next to a fireplace. And, true to French restaurant life, you get a fleeting glimpse of what's going on in the kitchen. They have an excellent wine selection as well as some cider and champagne. Highly recommend the "Mimi" with your galettes! About those galettes...mon dieu. Perfection. They are buckwheat crepes with savory ingredients inside. So, they are naturally gluten-free, and they have a few vegetarian options. I had the galette complete--a classic with ham, Gruyere, and egg. It tasted just like I remember when I lived in Nantes. My friend got the mushroom and cheese galette that has an amazing buttery texture. Couldn't ask for more. As for dessert, how could I not go for the classic buerre sucre crepe? Just butter and sugar, and it was perfect. No exaggerating. We also had a raspberry and lemon crepe at the table with a great balance of flavors. The lemon wasn't overpowering or too sweet. It was just right. And what can I say about the service? Everyone, and I mean everyone, was so nice and helpful. Shout out to Matt, our server, who was just as excited as we were about the food. The manager, Nicola, came by to tell us a bit about the restaurant and the food and seasonal menus that are coming up and took the time to let us know the hours. Obviously she could tell we will be regulars. And I even got to meet the owner and spout off some French with her. It was an enchanting dining experience, and I can't wait to go back for more. Take me back to France, Cropichon et Bidibule. We are going to be good friends.

If they ran out of the soup, that tells me that it's good and gives me a reason to go back already. The sandwich was creamy, gooey deliciousness! The salad was also a nice mix of spring greens, carrots, cherry tomatoes and cucumber with a vinagrette dressing served separately. For $9, it was a very generous plate of food...very, very GOOD food! My friend order the rotisserie chicken club sandwich with potato salad. It's great knowing that there's a quick and good lunch spot in Algiers that is within minutes of both home and the office. text: Yo! Sushi is a totally new concept for Tampa. It's conveyor-belt sushi also known as kaiten-sushi or kaiten-zushi or sushi-go-round in Japan. You sit at a booth and grab the sushi you want and pay at the end. My first experience with this kind of sushi was in San Francisco when I first tried sushi as a 5-year old at Isobune Sushi in Japantown and I have longed for a conveyor-belt style sushi place to come to Tampa since I moved here in 1999. Yo! Sushi is finally making that a reality. The style of Yo! Sushi is modern and different from Isobune. The focus is on fast, fresh, and convenient and the setup of the place follows this focus. When you walk-up to the restaurant it's open and easy to get a seat at. Call-buttons are placed at each table to make it easy to get service and close your check. Sushi is constantly being rolled and made by the sushi chefs at the restaurant and the open-kitchen let's you watch the chefs in action. I have faith a high-traffic area like the International Plaza will help ensure the freshness of the fish at Yo! Sushi. Plates range from $3-$6 and contain a variety of cooked and raw sushi, cooked Japanese food, and dessert. There's a little bit of something for everyone depending on your tastes. One of my favorite things I have tried so far is the Chicken Katsu Curry which comes a small plate with rice below and about 5 cuts of katsu for $5. I often want to order katsu at restaurants, but find it hard to justify spending $15 on dinner for one - especially when I also want sushi with my food and end up just ditching the katsu. This meets me halfway. As far as the sushi is concerned - it tastes fresh and is certainly above what you would find at a buffet or something like Koizi/Saki Endless Sushi. It's not quite the highest quality of sushi which is understandable considering the price and focus, but still satisfactory to me for the taste. Most of the sushi leans towards salmon, tuna, and imitation crab/crab special or California Roll-creations. I also liked the Popcorn Shrimp (tastes more like Bang Bang Shrimp), Takoyaki (hard to find a decent one in Tampa for sure!), and the Kimchi Salmon Steamed Bun (bun was just right and salmon pretty good quality!). There are plenty of things to try though so repeat visits will need to be made! For me, Yo! Sushi is great for a quick and tasty meal when I'm in a rush and don't necessarily want to spend as much time/money at a regular Japanese sushi restaurant. I can see how someone who wants a really high-end Japanese experience may not approve, but then one should also consider price and time into factors of that justification. The service is friendly/approachable and the managers clearly really love working for Yo! Sushi which is something plenty of restaurants in Tampa Bay seem to lack and may come from them being an international company. Definitely check it out even if it's just to try something new for fun with some friends or family. I know I'll be back often!

As for the cupcakes, we had the Chocolate Raspberry Gooey Butter, the Red Velvet, the Reese's, the Brownie, and the Carrot. All of them were great. There wasn't a miss in the whole bunch. The Gooey Butter had such a different texture than we have ever experienced. It's definitely the most unique of the cupcake options. The Red Velvet was good, but the filling tasted more like a dulce de leche than a caramel. The Carrot was also good, but we would have preferred there to be no coconut. Overall, this is a great cupcake place, but I am not sure how often we would go, since you are paying about $6 per cupcake.

text: When I lived in St. Louis for 3 years, several classmates recommended Greentree to me. My preferred mechanic was all the way in my home state of Florida so obviously that wasn't an option. I needed a mechanic in St. Louis. If someone was in St. Louis and was in need of a mechanic, here's what I would tell them about Greentree: -They are timely with repairs. -They are efficient at communicating with me over the phone and via email. -They have the customer convenience of usually having a loaner vehicle. -They have a comfortable waiting area. -They never made changes to the plan for my vehicle repairs without my consent first. -The lead mechanic is a great guy. All of these things are things that I value. And it should be noted that they are more expensive than any other mechanic I've been to, BUT they are also located in a place with a higher cost of living and therefore, their average customer can afford to pay the higher price at the neighborhood auto shop. This isn't all that outrageous. People should not be shocked by this. So why would I give this place 2 out of 5 stars? Because there is a HUGE problem with the way they do business. After getting them to install a tow package in my Jeep, three weeks later, crap hit the fan in my Jeep Grand Cherokee and they did NOT stand behind their work--more specifically behind the part that they placed in the vehicle. The NAPA Balkamp product they placed in my Jeep malfunctioned and caused an electrical fire in my vehicle. It was pretty serious, and it could have been a lot worse. My home-town, mechanic in Florida and the GEICO insurance rep both took one look at the NAPA part and identified that the fire started because the part malfunctioned. The damage was around $2,400. The insurance covered all except the $500 deductible. My mechanic, Dave, said that I should contact the mechanic in St. Louis (Greentree) that installed the part to cover the deductible. Dave said that he personally does business and that is industry standard. Because when you install a part, you're taking responsibility for it as the mechanic and if it malfunctions--he as the mechanic will take that up with the Rep he bought the part from. Why? Because I'm his customer and he is the customer of the auto parts distributor and their sales team. Dave has stood by his work on our family vehicles in this way for 20 years. Which is why we trust him and recommend him to everyone without hesitation. I do NOT put this same confidence in Greentree. When I called Greentree, they didn't take care of me--their customer. They passed the buck along to their NAPA Balkamp rep: Michael Mann. They gave me his number and I called him. I emailed him photos and texted them to him as well. Haven't heard back from him since we spoke in October 2014. Why? Well, because I'm not his customer--he doesn't care about me. If Jeff at Greentree came to him and said, "Hey this part you sold me caused my customer a huge problem--here's the scorched part to show you," then you better believe Michael Mann would have gotten back to him. But not me. Therefore, I paid the $500 deductible and I contacted Michael on three separate occasions and he hasn't gotten back to me. So...if you go to Greentree, be aware that if they place a part in your vehicle that malfunctions and causes any sort of damage, they will pass you along to their parts rep instead of taking care of you like they probably should. The hardest part of it all is this: I don't think the owner would do this to his pastor or his pastor's wife--who are customers there at Greentree. I don't think they would do this to any of the several area ministers who are also their patrons. But to an out of state graduate school student who's moving a 1000 miles away...well, it's easy to not deal with him like you would others because he's leaving town--so what does it matter?

text: Great neighborhood gem! When you order things you typically don't eat or like and find yourself a raving fan afterwards...that is the sign of a great chef. We had dinner for two on the patio. Our server was excellent and kept things flowing without hovering over us and provided excellent recommendations when asked. We started with the Buttonwood Farm turkey leg nachos and house smoked trout cake as appetizers and were impressed. I am not a huge fan of dark meat or sweet potato chips but this completely won me over as the flavor, balance, and presentation were all spot on. I envisioning ordering this again on my next visit. Similarly, the trout cakes were superb with a nice spice that paid compliments to the cake. For drinks, my dining companion ordered the Macklind Mule which was a balanced, refreshing drink that was truly enjoyable. I had Thomas Goss Cabernet that went well with the meal and something I would order again. Our entrees consisted of: 1) Circle B Farm heritage breed "Berkshire" pork chop* crispy lemon & Goatsbeard Farm goat cheese polenta cake * grilled Double Star Farms summer squash & bell peppers * basil cream * Scharf Farm smoked peach butter Everything on this entree was prepared to perfection and full of flavor. I sampled the chop and found it to be one of the most tender and moist meats I had ever eaten. Congratulations to the owners and chef for purchasing quality products and preparing them in a manner that truly embraces the essences of what Grapeseed is all about. I tip my hat to the chef for this meal. 2) Stuffed bell pepper w/ Buttonwood Farm smoked chicken * local zucchini summer yellow squash * Ozark Forest wild mushrooms * onion * roasted garlic Thies Farm heirloom tomato sauce * bed of wild rice * lemon-feta vinaigrette This was my entree and I don't care for stuffed peppers but I thought I would be adventurous and give it a try and I am glad I did. I fell in love with this meal from the first bite and was loath to share it with my dinner companion as I wanted to eat every morsel. Well prepared, bursting with flavor and filling without being stuffed (me, not the pepper). Every ingredient was fresh, well-made, and went well as a combination. We both agreed that on next return we would likely swap entrees as we both loved everything we tasted. Dessert was a bread pudding that would rival the best desserts in St. Louis. Full of flavor and make lite enough, for a bread pudding, that it didn't leave you feeling overfed. I had a berry dessert with some sort of sorbet that was passable and was the only thing I regretted. However the bread pudding was sufficient for the two of us and we make quick picking of it. Our experience was wonderful from seating, services, and dining. Grapeseed delivered at every spectrum of our expectations and we look forward to returning. Dinner for two including a generous tip was $154 I will return to the restaurant and highly recommend it to others.

As a "Top Chef" and Blais fan, I wanted it to be outstanding. I really tried. But with the loud music, absent waiting area and fair food, I won't be returning. Specifically, here's what didn't work for me: 1. Since it's a rainy day, the outdoor seating area was closed. My guess is this space is used for overflow for folks waiting for tables. Without that area, the tiny space in front of the host's stand (which inexplicably faces the bar instead of waiting guests) was crowded. 2. Other reviewers have noted the loud music, and I'll second/third/fourth their complaint. It's nearly as bad as Adele's sound quality, with the music video-playing TV's volume on blast in the dining area. 2. There were nine beers on draught, and they only had three of them. They didn't say if they were out or if those supplies haven't yet arrived -- the restaurant's only been open a week -- and those beers they did have weren't all that appealing or local. 3. I ordered the fauxlafel (chickpea, arugula, cucumber, pickled beets, red onion, tzatziki yogurt spread) on a lettuce wrap instead of a bun, which is an option I was glad to see. I expected to be able to pick it up and eat it with my hands; you know, like a lettuce wrap. Instead, the burger was placed atop a wedge of lettuce, so I had to eat it with a knife and a fork. This isn't a minus -- yet the burger was so dry that it crumbled eat time I tried to stab it with the fork. The flavors were nice, and I liked the crisp lettuce against the yogurt spread. 4. My husband's bison burger tasted like an elementary school's sloppy joe. It was messy, fell apart and not special. I'm surprised this came from Blais's genius mind; maybe I don't understand it yet? Maybe there are hidden chemical compounds that will burst with flavor in our mouths overnight? Doubtful. Here's what I thought was grand: 1. The beef fat french fries come with smoked mayo and ketchup as dipping sauces, and the smoked mayo is excellent. Why have we been dipping into ketchup for so long while this existed in the world? I'm someone who orders truffle fries and regrets it -- They're greasy and not worth the extra couple dollars. Here, the beef fat was light, and the flavor's worth it. 2. The milkshakes are delicious. They leave no coating on the roof of your mouth, and are hit-the-spot cold. I had the foie gras milkshake -- yep, that's right; only Blais -- and the server (who had a great personality/disposition) said I'm the first to order it from her. They melt the foie gras down before blending it, and there are small, delicious pebbles of it mixed through the shake. Small bits of doughnut rested in my husband's Krispy Kreme milkshake. There was more "eh" than "yum!" in our visit this afternoon (around 2:30 on a rainy Sunday with a 25-minute wait), so we're unlikely to return.

text: Diner en Blanc 2015 was my first time and definitely going to be my last. From what I've gathered, previous years were unique, classy experiences that people raved over. We got to the meeting place at 6 as specified and waited...and waited for 45 minutes to get the go ahead to get started. We took a reserved subway car (this was a nice touch and well handled) to the end of the line and then walked a little over a mile to the Navy Yard...which was pretty underwhelming. Has anyone not already been to an event at the Navy Yard? We set up in a field that you literally can rent to hold your wedding reception, if you didn't really care to have a distinctive event. Probably due to the weather, it was dark and the planners didn't set up adequate lighting. We weren't among the lucky ones that were near one of the lights, so it was difficult to see and thus set up our tables. At one point, one of the organizers came over, carrying an enormous umbrella. For some reason, instead of taking a few steps to the side to go around our group to get to the other end, he bulled right through where everyone was setting up, hitting everyone he walked past/through with his umbrella. He didn't acknowledge this or apologize for it, but at least he did raise it higher so he was no longer hitting people. We got the catering by Palladino. As I said before, the lighting was very poor, so it was very difficult to see what we were eating and what we got was bland. It's hard to speak to this, because it's not my thing, but a drag queen singing in an...okay...voice wasn't what I would have expected for an event like this. To sum up, it was around $160 for the event itself, plus all the cost and hassle of getting the clothes and items for it, for an event that wouldn't even rank into the top 5 wedding receptions I've been to...held at the Navy Yard. text: Executive summary: this is the most UnHamptonish Hampton Inn I've ever stayed in. So keep this in mind - you may not share my rating, but you'll likely agree with the statement. My company strongly endorses Hampton Inn for business trips. For many of my co-workers, this is fine as it is apparently the ground floor of what they consider to be an acceptable hotel. I personally find them sterile and conformist, and well over the price range of what I'd ever pay for personal lodging. (I'm more a hostel/quirky dive motel type.) So it was we checked into this place and had differing opinions. Almost every HI I've stayed in is cookie-cutter assembled (maybe from the same machine they bake their evening cookies in?), 3-story buildings with hallways and lame attempts at dry humor. This one is obviously a property that the chain bought and generally left as is. Here's their/my takes: The rooms all open to the outside, are two-story, and the building makes up an immense rectangle centered around a gigantic pool area (half the rooms being pool view, half being parking lot). I have no qualms whatsoever with external, but it is apparently a very big deal to some. The rooms are generally kept up, though maybe they could stand a fresh coat of paint or some work around the tub. Not that that bothers me in the slightest, but it might you and it certainly didn't escape their attention. More concerning was one guy who saw a roach in his room, and another who had a running toilet in his. But I had no issues with mine, and I'm the one writing the review. I did love the bamboo window blinds, a tiki touch. The thing I loved about this place was the pool area, complete with hot tub and another tiki-ish waterfall. The huge pool is heated also, though on the 50-degree evening I was there not heated enough. The hot tub was great, though, and it was overall a great old-school Florida feel and a vibe totally absent from yr typical Hampton. My co-workers were anxious to book a different hotel on future visits, whereas I thought this was the only hotel with character during our weeklong Hampton-heavy tour through Florida. So it is that I give an inconceivable 4-star rating to this place, because it is the one Hampton you'll remember no matter what - and for this ordinarily faceless chain, that's saying something.
label: POS

text: Sounds like the place recently got new management and is going downhill. To be fair, the only thing I ended up getting there was a Bloody Mary, so I won't comment on the food. What I will comment on is how disappointingly the situation there was handled by the staff and why we decided not to eat there. If you go to the following address off The Kitchen's website (unless they finally take down the page), you'll notice some really tasty-sounding food items for Sundays under the "Sunday Hangover Brunch" http://kitchenstpete.com/food/sunday/ Well, too bad they no longer do the Sunday Hangover Brunch. When we asked why it's still on their website, we were told because the new management hasn't gotten around to taking it off yet. They also had a poster with the info right in front of the entrance. So we ask if there's any way they can whip up at least something similar to what was advertised, and the waitress disappears for several minutes to try and track down the chef (maybe she should have tracked down a manager, if there was one around?) Then she comes back and says "Do you guys wanna go ahead and order any food?". My fiance and I look at each other, kind of surprised, and try to explain we're wanting to see what feedback we get on the brunch stuff. It became obvious that our waitress really couldn't give a f***, and was just annoyed because it seemed to her we were just campers. After 20 minutes, NO ONE came out, which really suggests to me a lack of active management presence. Here's the thing - let's say a manager HAD come out. Even if they could do nothing other than offer their apologies and indicate they'd work to get the bogus advertisement for the Brunch down quickly, I would have been satisfied with the situation and willing to try something else on their menu. I don't mind when things go wrong, I mind when the response is poor and non receptive to the customer. It seems clear that this place is hindered by poor management and lackluster staff. Their food may be good (their Bloody Mary was very decent), but there are a lot of places I can spend my money that also have good food and likely have better management than this place. I'd steer clear and spend your money elsewhere so bad customer service is not supported.

text: I have hemmed and hawed about writing this review for 6 months now. I don't want to throw the stylist under the bus because I do like her as a person, so I won't name her, but it's something that is still bothering me so I decided to go ahead and write the review. PULL UP A CHAIR, KIDS. IT'S A LONG ONE. I moved here from out of state and needed a new stylist. Serenity was close, so I went there. I've had black hair for 10 years and wanted to gradually go back to a dark brown/auburn. She decided the best way would be to put highlights through the length, and color my roots lighter as they come in. So, she did that the first couple times, and then at that point I realized because I don't know anyone here, and have no social life, there's really no point in spending so much money when I don't go anywhere anyway (despite being in a strip mall, the prices are less like the typical shops that occupy these spaces, and closer to actual spa salons.) So, from 11/2013 to 12/2014 I just let it grow again (from a badly botched haircut a few years ago, of course) and colored my roots at home. In December I decided to start, you know, making an effort to get out of the depression this move has put me in, and went in to start getting my hair done again. I still wanted to end up closer to natural, so she put fresh highlights in and while she was doing my color I asked if she had any recommendations for someone I could go to for a Brazilian Blowout, since I knew they didn't do them. She didn't, but asked why I didn't just get a keratin treatment, because they do those. I said I hate the 3 day waiting period. She said their keratin treatment is only a 24 hour wait before being able to wash it out. I decided to go ahead and make an appt for that for 2 weeks later. On Christmas Eve I showed up for my appt, super excited that my hair was FINALLY back to the really long length I was trying to get back to, and that I was well on my way to getting the end result I was aiming for. I had been really paranoid about the damage highlights and the soap cap would do to my already-weirdly-textured hair, but I ended up pretty happy with it, and there was no noticeable damage at all (HOORAY!) My hair loves keratin treatments and I knew it would be even better after this appt, and I was finally getting out of this 1.5+ year long funk this move had put me in. So, my hair was clarified, and the treatment was put on. Then she said it was time to go rinse it out. Er..you don't rinse keratin treatments out. And then she put a neutralizer in. I asked what brand it was, because all the keratin I've done (and I've done many) do not have rinse-outs or neutralizers. You clarify/dry/apply keratin/dry/flatiron and don't touch for 3 days. She said it was Matrix. I said that years ago I used to get the Matrix Opti-Smooth. She said "That's what this is, with keratin." THIS IS NOT A KERATIN TREATMENT. And what popped into my head immediately was how years ago when I used to get it done I had to have highlight extensions put in when I wanted highlights, because you shouldn't do them both together because your hair will break. But I figured she knew what she was doing, even though this wasn't a keratin treatment--- it's a chemical straightener. One coats and improves hair's texture. The other breaks the bonds, and essentially destroys it. After it was dried/styled it was sooooo dry and crunchy. It was awful. I went home and it was snapping off everywhere. My highlights were completely elastic. I spent a lot more money on strengtheners and deep conditioners. After a bit, I called and said my hair is fried, and I realized that I had paid someone to DAMAGE my hair. She said we must've had a ~miscommunication~ because she looked into keratin afterward and it's like a Brazilian Blowout-- CONVENIENTLY FORGETTING THAT *SHE* SUGGESTED THIS WHEN I WAS ASKING ABOUT BRAZILIAN BLOWOUTS. She already knew this! Long story short (loljk), she refunded my $100 for the second appt, but I am still out what I paid for my highlights and color 2 weeks prior, along with all the conditioners and treatments I've tried. I drove 5 hours back to MI to beg my old stylist to see what she could do. Her treatment (more$) helped, but not enough. She cut off 8 inches of my finally-newly-long-again hair. It should've been even more, but I couldn't bear to have it any shorter. I need it long enough to clip up, because that's what I have to do every single day now. Every 10 weeks I drive the 5 hours back to her and she cuts a couple more inches off, because with each cut I just get new completely fried, scraggly ends, since the entire shaft is damaged. Half a year later I still have broken pieces everywhere. It's still breaking off. It's going to be another 4 years before I have long, healthy hair and all of this is gone. Again.

The same thing with the self serve popcorn from the machine. The small pointy cups were there to make sure you don't take to much (usually there are baskets with some type of wax paper so you can share it with your friends). Even the popcorn tasted stale, like it was popped hours ago. Welcome to Ds! The bartender took our order - bourbon Manhattan and Makers on the rocks. Drinks were good - bartender seemed unhappy unless dealing with one of the many regulars. A waitress took our food order and billed us just for food. Who does that? Maybe ordering drinks and food is too complicated. I have no idea why. My girlfriend ordered the shrimp wrapped in bacon and a Caesar salad. I ordered a house favorite - chicken parmigiana with spaghetti. It came with a salad. The shrimp was good as you would expect when bacon is involved. Decent size. The Caesar salad was ok - the dressing was not typical and lettuce not crisp. The chicken parm was a huge disappointment. It was obviously not pounded out then pan fried the way great chicken parm is cooked. The spaghetti sauce tasted like it came from a jar. The salad I received was iceberg and odds and ends thrown together. Didn't touch it. The garlic bread was like the kind you cook in a tin bag. Read the review Steve S wrote for an deeper understanding of this local institution. Lucky for me, I have not been here for banquets or dinners. I doubt I'll be coming back and if I do, it will be for drinks. The food was nothing special.

text: This is my 3rd trip to the Yard House. We come here because my wife likes it, not because I do. read on to learn why Im not a fan. The Yard House is in "The Village." The Village reminds me of that old TV series "The Prisoner". http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061287 For those out there that are older, like me, you might remember "The Prisoner". But then again, it did not get a huge amount of play time here in the US. The TV series was set in a place called "The Village", which was a very secretive and isolated community for people that the government needed disappeared. The entire show was about this one ex-MI6 agent that the leaders of The Village were trying to get secrets out of. It was a really cool, but also very bizarre British TV series. I will give 1 example of it bizarreness. When the Prisoner tried to escape, a huge ball (about 6 feet around) named Rover would come rolling down the street. It would roll over the Prisoner and envelop his face. When it did, he screamed in pain. I am not exactly sure why our Village reminds me of this old show. Perhaps its the layout and design that is reminiscent of The Village. Perhaps its the way that The Village in Meridian is a little on the secretive and exclusive side of things. Maybe its because The Village is just too upscale of me. I am more of a plane Tee shirt sort of guy that likes his plain old meat and potatoes. I am not exactly sure, but for whatever reason, this place gives me the Willies. Well, on with the review. This place in Noisy. The music is loud. The main theme here is Alcohol. The bar is huge and take center stage right smack in the middle of the place. Now that I think on this, this probably one of the reasons Im not comfortable here. I am not a drinker, though I do have a mixed drink on occasion. When I was here, most every table had Alcohol in one form or another on it. The smell of Alcohol permeates the entire place. The Yard House is a huge bar. Perhaps the yard House is the waive of the future. No longer does the hostess have to ask if you want to sit at the bar or in the dining area. Places like the Yard House no longer give you that choice. Either you sit where there is liquor being served, or you find another place to eat. The Yard House is not a family friendly place. Alcohol is everywhere you look. But this does not seem to stop families from coming here. I noticed more than a few examples of this. A family with 2 or 3 kids at the table with mom and dad. The kids were eating burgers and fries while mom and dad were guzzling beer and wine. A picture that you would never see in my family growing up, and will never see in my family now. I would call this place a Basteraunt or a Restaubar. Like most every other place in The Village, the prices here are on the high side. This is another reason why The Yard House is not Family Friendly. My small family of 3 paid $42, which is on the lower end of an average ticket price here. The last 2 times I was at the Yard House, I had a burger. The burgers here are pretty good, when they are good. Like so many places though, its hit or miss depending on who cooks it and perhaps what mood they were in that day. This time, i had Street Tacos. I did like these, but 3 of them came no where close to filling me up. In fact, I told my wife that the 3 tacos were a cute Amuse-bouche (Appetizer). Now I was ready for my main meal. After we ate here, we went to Fast Freddie's for a hamburger. I am not a fan of the yard House. If you are a drinker, you might well like it here. There is lots and lots of booze here. If like me, you dont like being around alcohol and dont want your kids exposed to alcohol, you will want to find yourself another place to eat.

text: I highly recommend visiting the newly opened Tinker Street and soon! I just don't see how you could possibly leave disappointed. I have been excited for Tinker Street to open for a very long time. Located at 16th and New Jersey, I live 6 blocks away. It was almost a year ago that announcements were made about this wonderful establishment opening in the near future. INTERIOR: First of all, space is limited. It is a small restaurant, but they made great use of the smaller space. We dined inside. The interior is intimate, inviting and very urban. The enclosed patio looked just as inviting (and warm on a frigid January night). LOCATION: This area really needed some new restaurants, so Tinker Street is a very welcomed addition! PARKING: They have their own parking lot! Major bonus. Tons of free street parking nearby as well. SERVICE: Impeccable. These folks know what they are doing! DRINK MENU: Excellent wine offerings. A wine specialist visited our table right away, poured us a miniature glass of Prosecco (as a "thank you" for coming in) and then proceeded to answer our questions about the wine list, make suggestions, etc. Very impressed. The rotating beer selection is mostly local and great. DINNER MENU: There is certainly something for every appetite and diet here. Plates are smaller and very "foodie" like, so it is great to go with others and share. We had the following: Hummus Lemon Oil, Dried Olive and Pita ($6) - Not the best hummus I have had in town, but it was good. We ran out of pita chips and it was nice to know that we could request extra. Fried Brussels Sprouts, Dukhah Spice and Dijon Vinaigrette ($6). - Very tasty with amazing flavor, but maybe not the best option if you are trying to dine healthy. They are fried, but well worth it on a cheat day or a splurge! Fresh Pappardelle Tomato Ragu with House Made Herb Ricotta ($13) - Excellent vegetarian dish. Yet, I would have loved some meat on it and will ask if this is an option next visit. Still very delish! Albacore Tuna Celeriac, Kale and Pomegranate Molasses Vinaigrarette ($18)- OUTSTANDING!!! OTHER NOTES: The staff at Tinker Street is extremely friendly. Again, these folks know what they are doing. Top notch service. This is a 21 and over establishment for those of you that may want to bring children. Further, I hear they will not be allowing pets on the patio when weather permits and they open the patio. Just some "good to know" info! I can't wait to go back or to hear about these happy hour specials they will be sharing soon!

text: Being born and raised in Georgia sets the bar pretty high on a few different categories in life and BBQ is no exception to that rule. I got there about 12:30, at the height of the lunch rush, and by then they had already sold out of the ribs and chicken. This gem makes all the food they are going to have that day, and when it's gone, it's really gone so get there early! I got the regular size pulled pork sandwich and my lunch buddy got the jumbo lunch plate that came with 2 sides and a drink. The jumbo size is a HUGE portion of meat on a large bun that made me glad I got the smaller size. The baked beans were good, but nothing too special. They had a little sweetness to them with a little bit of pulled pork added in, and the potato salad was also tasty. It wasn't too wet and had a little bit of mustard and relish added in. All in all it is a great place for delicious bbq when you're down in the St. Pete/Clearwater area! I'll definitely be back, just much earlier next time since I want to try some ribs!

I tensed up a lot to give her the signal that it was uncomfortable and unwelcome but she was just like, "Oh, you're tense here," and dug in more. She shorted me 10 minutes. Not that I can say I'm too upset for the massage to have come to an end, but I did pay for the full 90 minutes. Don't go here. Just don't do it. Oh how I wish I had consulted yelp before my visit here. Never again will I step foot in this place.

text: Eating here was the worst seafood experience of my life! I ordered the KJ Steampot with snow crab, seared scallops and mussels, and I also added a lobster on the side for a total of over $50. Hey, this is Indiana, so if I want to eat a platter of amazing seafood, I'm prepared to pay a high price. When the steam pot came out it looked beautiful. The crab, mussels and tiny scallops were wrapped in a green net over a whole cob of corn and potatoes. The lobster came out separately with several ramekins of butter. I was so excited... Then I smelled it and the putrid stench of something that reminded me of formaldehyde overtook me. See, I've worked in biology labs where we use formaldehyde to keep dead animals from decaying so we can dissect them, and one of the worst parts of the job is smelling the harmful chemical (which can cause coma and death among other implications if ingested). Why did my food smell like formaldehyde? Feeling a burning sensation in my stomach after eating my crab, scallops and half my lobster, I looked up why my food could possibly smell and taste like formaldehyde, and it turns out after crustaceans die (e.g. crab and lobster) some of the chemicals in their body begin to turn into formaldehyde! This occurs over time even if the crustaceans are frozen but isn't noticeable unless the food has been dead for quite some time. I tried eating the corn and potatoes but after being nauseated by the seafood they tasted just as stingily putrid because of the steaming process. I asked the waitress Jessica if they were fresh or frozen and she confirmed they were frozen. I asked how long they were frozen and informed her I was seriously feeling nauseous but she just told me I was probably over thinking it. With my science background -- of course I was! And for the good of future customers. I never got a clear answer on how long their seafood is frozen before it was thawed and served, but I am concerned it was far too long to meet health and safety regulations. If crabs and lobsters are kept frozen too long, they become a health hazard and can make you sick which was my experience. This location was awesome when it first opened but is now on its last crabby legs and keeps its stockpile of relatively 'fresh' seafood in the freezer far too long because of its lack of business to be healthy or appetizing. For your own health, please avoid eating here!

text: It is very rare that you get to write a review of an institution that has actually saved your life. At the age of thirteen I was diagnosed with a brain tumor and underwent brain surgery at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. The hospital has won many awards and accolades since its establishment, and I personally never received anything but the best of care while a patient. CHOP, as its more commonly known, admits more than 15,000 children each year; if the President's children were sick, they would probably be patients at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. If nothing else, I'm grateful my parents were able to get me the best medical attention possible. There is no doubt in my mind that a lesser hospital, employing less skilled surgeons, would have left me severely brain damaged, or worse. Once arriving at CHOP, my parents, grief-stricken upon learning of my diagnoses, immediately calmed down. The doctors and nurses had a great bedside manner, the perfect mixture of comfort and professionalism. I remember very little from the day of my surgery. An IV was stuck into my arm and an anesthesiologist sedated me. My neurosurgeon was Doctor Suttor, chief of the neurosurgery division at CHOP. I regained consciousness a few hours later, back in my hospital room. The surgery was a success. When I woke back up I wanted nothing more than a cool drink of water. The doctors forbid me from drinking liquids and I had to be content with ice chips. My head pounded and my hair had been shaved during the surgery. There were twenty staples in the back of my head and all of them itched like hell. After the surgery, I couldn't control the entire right side of my body. It was almost as if I had a stroke, except my right arm and leg shook constantly and uncontrollably. There were bed rails on either side of the hospital bed, as if I were a toddler who just graduated from his crib. It's not easy to get much sleep while you're in a hospital. As tired as I was, I couldn't get any rest. During those few times I was able to fall asleep naturally I would soon be woken up. A nurse would barge into my room, stick me with a needle, and shine a light in my eyes. In the days that followed I regained some control over the right side of my body. My limbs still shook constantly, but now I was able do things like hold a pencil or stand up while leaning against something for support. A physical therapist came by one day and I took my first steps outside the hospital room. My tumor was located in the cerebellum--the part of your brain that controls balance and motor skills, among other things. During such an invasive surgery there's bound to be some brain damage. It's no surprise that I was having trouble with walking and coordination. Immediately after the surgery, there was also concern I'd suffer from memory loss--the cerebellum also controls some cognitive functioning, like attention and memory. Fortunately, I was untouched mentally, but trapped inside a body my brain could no longer control. I was only able to walk on my own by using a gait belt to help with balance. Even then, I couldn't take more than ten steps at a time. A doctor came into the hospital room one day and handed me a plastic medical bag. Inside the hermetically sealed bag was the tumor they cut out of my head. My tumor was the size of a golf ball and pink like a wad of bubble gum. It felt empowering to hold in my hand what had once tried to kill me. I was able to hold down Italian water ice, but little else. I remember trying to eat an orange and vomiting all over myself after the first bite. I can't speak to the quality of hospital food, as even the smell turned my stomach. There was a bootlegger outside the hospital who sold VHS copies of movies still in their theatrical run, or not yet released on home video. My parents bought me a few tapes to play on the VCR in my hospital room. I think Titanic was the first movie I watched after the surgery. I could only handle watching television in fifteen-minute increments, so it took a long time before I finished the entire three-hour movie. There was a McDonald's in the basement of CHOP. I never understood why they let the world's unhealthiest fast food restaurant open up a location in a hospital; maybe they thought sick children wouldn't feel so bad if they were eating a happy meal. On my last day in the hospital I ordered a sausage and egg McMuffin with cheese. I ate the breakfast sandwich, a side of hash browns, and was able to keep everything down. It was a personal triumph. If I was able to handle the greasiest food in the world, there was a chance I wouldn't starve and waste away. All told, I spent a total of two weeks in the hospital. I was given the option of staying at CHOP and continuing my physical therapy there, but I opted to go back home and receive treatment at a local facility.

text: I hate to give such a negative review because this place seemed to have potential, and in general I am not a negative person. After years of knowing about this spot I decided to give it a try while I had a visitor in town. Upon entering the restaurant on a Tuesday it was packed! We walked straight through to the patio which had a high volume of customers. It took virtually 20 minutes before we were even looked at. There were two main severs covering (running around) the entire wraparound patio. Our server was doing the best she could and was very pleasant once we received service. Once acknowledged we put in a few appetizer orders. We had the saganaki and the horta (endive greens). The saganaki was pleasantly toasted on the outside and gooey on the inside. As our server ignited it with Ouzo table side, it made quite the attraction for those around us who noticed and delighted in the spectacle. The horta lacked flavor but came out in a large portion which was good. For lunch we had the lunch specials. I decided to go with the "fish special" as it is labeled on the menu and not specified as a sandwich abc start off with a Greek salad. The Greek salad was not seemingly as fresh or of the quality I had had at a neighboring restaurant and the potato salad plopped on the center tasted like it wasn't make with real mayo but who am I to judge? When asked what kind of fish it was I was told it was cod however when the meal came out as a sandwich I identified the fish as a flounder type, as I have eaten seafood my whole life and are able to discern the difference. Perhaps the server didn't know what type of fish it was or as was misinformed. The bun was fresh although I didn't eat it and it came with some nice tomato slices. My sister had the spanakopita and it, although tasty was thin. The dessert that came with the lunch specials that day was galactobourekou. The farina/custard filling itself was a bit soft and very sweet. The syrup used was nice, though, and luckily it was only a little piece because I felt compelled to eat it all. I must say that I made use of the women's restroom when I was there and it was clean and the decor was pleasant and there was a candle burning if I remember correctly which I thought was a nice touch. I recommend having more servers during the weekday lunch rush if it is a trend that the resturant is normally busy. The servers that you have work hard and are diligent but they can only do so much. Sadly I have to say, I probably will not be returning but I hope for the best for this place because it seems like a mainstay on the Tarpon scene. I would like to chalk up my experience to a bad day. I would give 2.5 stars if I could. If anything, the server redeemed some of the negative aspects as she was doing her best it seemed and the food wasn't entirely bad.
